revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Cookie Houses
revealWordProblem.text:
A cookie house building kit contains three different cookie house kits. The finished houses are labeled A, B, and C, and the flat cookie pieces that fold up to make them are labeled 1, 2, and 3.
Question: Which flat kit matches which cookie house? Explain your reasoning.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: Three finished cookie houses labeled A, B, and C beside three flat nets labeled 1, 2, and 3.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Match each net to a house by counting and naming the faces. Count how many flat pieces each net has and what shape each one is, then check whether the finished house needs exactly those faces — a house with a peaked roof needs triangles, a box-shaped house needs six rectangles, and a pyramid-shaped house needs one base with triangles all around it. Fold each net mentally (or on paper) to confirm the pieces meet edge to edge with no overlap. The match is right when the number of faces, the shape of each face, and the way they fold all agree.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — How do we find the surface area of a box?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. So we go up a level, not up a number: find what is always true, show it a second way, and be ready to defend it with a reason instead of an answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: A box has 3 pairs of matching faces, so add up all 6 faces to get the surface area — and you can say why it is true, and where it would stop being true.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My box is 8 in. long, 5 in. wide, and 3 in. tall. I unfold it into a net and see 3 pairs of faces.
Top and bottom: each is 8 × 5 = 40, and there are 2 of them, so 2 × 40 = 80.
Front and back: each is 8 × 3 = 24, so 2 × 24 = 48.
Left and right: each is 5 × 3 = 15, so 2 × 15 = 30.
I add all the pairs: 80 + 48 + 30 = 158. The surface area is 158 in².
linesEs: Mi caja mide 8 pulg de largo, 5 pulg de ancho y 3 pulg de alto. La desdoblo en una plantilla y veo 3 pares de caras.
Arriba y abajo: cada una es 8 × 5 = 40, y hay 2, así que 2 × 40 = 80.
Frente y atrás: cada una es 8 × 3 = 24, así que 2 × 24 = 48.
Izquierda y derecha: cada una es 5 × 3 = 15, así que 2 × 15 = 30.
Sumo todos los pares: 80 + 48 + 30 = 158. El área de superficie es 158 pulg².

weDo.title: Try it together — then prove it
lines: Now a smaller box: 4 long, 3 wide, 2 tall. How many pairs of faces does it have?
Top and bottom: 4 × 3 = 12, times 2 = 24. Front and back: 4 × 2 = 8, times 2 = 16.
Left and right: 3 × 2 = 6, times 2 = 12. Now add 24 + 16 + 12. What is the surface area?
Yes, SA = 52 in². Remember to use square units.
Now prove it: say why that move had to work at all — not just that it did.
Sentence frame — convince a skeptic: "My method works because ___ . It would stop working if ___ ."
linesEs: Ahora una caja más pequeña: 4 de largo, 3 de ancho, 2 de alto. ¿Cuántos pares de caras tiene?
Arriba y abajo: 4 × 3 = 12, por 2 = 24. Frente y atrás: 4 × 2 = 8, por 2 = 16.
Izquierda y derecha: 3 × 2 = 6, por 2 = 12. Ahora suma 24 + 16 + 12. ¿Cuál es el área de superficie?
Sí, 52 pulg². Recuerda usar unidades cuadradas.
Ahora demuéstralo: di por qué ese paso tenía que funcionar — no solo que funcionó.
Marco de oración — convence a alguien que duda: «Mi método funciona porque ___ . Dejaría de funcionar si ___ .»

youDo.title: Now you try — and defend it
lines: Try the problems below on your own. Getting the answer is half the work — be ready to say why your method works, and where it would stop working.
Then pick one problem and show it a second way. If two different methods agree, that agreement is your proof.
linesEs: Intenta los problemas de abajo por tu cuenta. Obtener la respuesta es la mitad del trabajo — prepárate para decir por qué funciona tu método y dónde dejaría de funcionar.
Luego elige un problema y muéstralo de una segunda manera. Si dos métodos distintos coinciden, esa coincidencia es tu prueba.

onLevel.stem: A cube has edges of 5 cm. What is its surface area?
onLevel.explanation: A cube has 6 identical faces. Each face: 5 × 5 = 25 cm². Total SA = 6 × 25 = 150 cm².
choiceFeedback: Square the edge length for one face's area first, then multiply by the number of faces.
That's the volume calculation (edge cubed) — surface area needs six face areas added together.
Check the units — a flat surface is measured in square units, not cubic.

onLevel.explanationEs: Un cubo tiene 6 caras idénticas. Cada cara: 5 × 5 = 25 cm². Área total de la superficie = 6 × 25 = 150 cm².
hintsEs: Las 6 caras de un cubo son cuadrados idénticos, cada uno de 5 cm por 5 cm.

onLevel.prompt: Two boxes have the same volume of 60 in³. Box A is 5 × 4 × 3. Box B is 10 × 6 × 1. Which box uses less wrapping paper (has less surface area)? Show your calculations and explain why a more cube-like shape might use less material.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: Box A: SA = 2(___) + 2(___) + 2(___) = ___ in². Box B: SA = 2(___) + 2(___) + 2(___) = ___ in². Box ___ uses less wrapping paper because ___.
onLevel.hint: Find the surface area of each shape, then compare the totals.
hints: Both boxes hold 60 in³, but wrapping paper depends on SURFACE AREA — the outside covering, not the inside space.
Compute SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh for each box, then compare the two totals before you explain.
Box A first: faces are 5×4 = 20, 5×3 = 15, and 4×3 = 12. Double each and add, then repeat for Box B's faces.
onLevel.explanation: Both boxes hold 60 in³, but wrapping paper is measured by surface area. Box A: 2(20) + 2(15) + 2(12) = 94 in². Box B: 2(60) + 2(10) + 2(6) = 152 in². Box A uses less paper because its dimensions are closer to a cube — flattening the same volume into 10 × 6 × 1 creates two huge 60 in² faces and a lot of extra covering.
onLevel.explanationEs: Las dos cajas contienen 60 in³, pero el papel de regalo se mide con el área de superficie. Box A: 2(20) + 2(15) + 2(12) = 94 in². Box B: 2(60) + 2(10) + 2(6) = 152 in². Box A usa menos papel porque sus dimensiones se parecen más a un cubo; aplanar el mismo volumen hasta 10 × 6 × 1 crea dos caras enormes de 60 in² y mucho más que cubrir.
onLevel.promptEs: Dos cajas tienen el mismo volumen de 60 in³. La caja A mide 5 × 4 × 3. La caja B mide 10 × 6 × 1. ¿Cuál caja usa menos papel de envolver (tiene menos área superficial)? Muestra tus cálculos y explica por qué una forma más parecida a un cubo puede usar menos material.
hintsEs: Ambas cajas contienen 60 pulg³, pero el papel de regalo depende del ÁREA SUPERFICIAL: la cubierta exterior, no el espacio interior.
Calcula AS = 2la + 2lh + 2ah para cada caja y luego compara los dos totales antes de explicar.
Caja A primero: las caras son 5×4 = 20, 5×3 = 15 y 4×3 = 12. Duplica cada una y suma; luego repite con las caras de la Caja B.

Box C: 2(60) + 2(24) + 2(10) = 188 ft². The answers carry square units because you are covering the outside, not filling the inside.
extending.explanationEs: El área de superficie suma las seis caras, así que usa SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh en cada fila. Box A: 2(60) + 2(40) + 2(24) = 248 in². Box B: 2(49) + 2(21) + 2(21) = 182 cm². Box C: 2(60) + 2(24) + 2(10) = 188 ft². Las respuestas llevan unidades cuadradas porque estás cubriendo el exterior, no llenando el interior.

hintsEs: Cada fila necesita el ÁREA SUPERFICIAL, no el volumen: el área total de las seis caras, en unidades cuadradas.
Usa AS = 2la + 2lh + 2ah en cada fila: tres áreas de cara, cada una duplicada y luego sumadas.
Caja A: las caras son 10×6 = 60, 10×4 = 40 y 6×4 = 24. Duplica cada una y luego suma los resultados.

extending.label: A gift box has SA = 222 in². The top and bottom together are 120 in². The front and back together are 60 in². How much area is the left and right sides together?
extending.questionText: What is the combined area of the left and right faces?
extending.hint: Subtract the face areas you already know from the total surface area.
hints: The total SA (222 in²) is split into three face pairs. Two pairs are known: 120 in² and 60 in².
Subtract the known pairs from the total — whatever is left must belong to the left and right sides.
Add the known pairs first: 120 + 60 = 180 in². Then find how far 180 is from 222.
extending.explanation: The three face pairs together make up the entire surface area. The top-and-bottom pair (120 in²) plus the front-and-back pair (60 in²) accounts for 180 in², so the left and right faces must cover whatever is left: 222 − 180 = 42 in².
extending.explanationEs: Los tres pares de caras juntos forman toda el área de superficie. El par de arriba y abajo (120 in²) más el par del frente y el fondo (60 in²) suma 180 in², así que las caras izquierda y derecha deben cubrir lo que falta: 222 − 180 = 42 in².
hintsEs: El AS total (222 pulg²) se divide en tres pares de caras. Dos pares son conocidos: 120 pulg² y 60 pulg².
Resta los pares conocidos del total: lo que sobre debe pertenecer a los lados izquierdo y derecho.
Suma primero los pares conocidos: 120 + 60 = 180 pulg². Luego encuentra qué tan lejos está 180 de 222.

extending.stem: You unfold a time capsule that is a cube. Its net shows 6 equal squares, and each square has an area of 4 cm². What is the cube's total surface area?
extending.explanation: A cube net has 6 equal square faces. With each face 4 cm², the surface area is 6 × 4 = 24 cm².
choiceFeedback: Multiply the face area by all six faces — don't just add the face count to the area.
Some faces are easy to forget in a net — make sure you count and include all six squares.
A cube net has six faces, not four — multiply the face area by six.
extending.stemEs: Desdoblas una cápsula del tiempo que tiene forma de cubo. Su desarrollo plano muestra 6 cuadrados iguales, y cada cuadrado tiene un área de 4 cm². ¿Cuál es el área total de la superficie del cubo?
extending.explanationEs: El desarrollo plano de un cubo tiene 6 caras cuadradas iguales. Con cada cara de 4 cm², el área de la superficie es 6 × 4 = 24 cm².
hints: A net shows every face of the solid laid out flat, so the surface area is simply the total of all the face areas.
The faces of a cube are all identical, so instead of adding six different numbers you can use repeated addition or multiplication.
Each square is 4 cm² and the net shows 6 of them, so set up 6 groups of 4 cm² and finish the multiplication.
